## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 63, titled *Ukkoṭana* ("Reopening a settled legal issue"), regulates the offense of reopening or agitating an issue of monastic law (*adhikaraṇa*) that has already been formally and lawfully settled [SuttaCentral; Dutt 1957]. According to the rule (*yo pana bhikkhu jānaṁ yathādhammam nihitādhikaraṇaṁ punakammāya ukkoṭeyya pācittiyaṁ*), a monk who knowingly seeks to reopen such a settled case for further formal legal proceedings incurs an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) requiring confession [SuttaCentral; Dutt 1957; Vinaya Pitaka vol 4]. In monastic jurisprudence, the rule operates to safeguard the finality of Sangha decisions against contentious monks who create strife and prolong disputes [Dutt 1957; Vinaya Pitaka vol 4]. An English translation has been provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral], and the rule is noted in comparative studies of monastic disciplinary codes [Clarke 2014].

Parallels to the rule exist extensively across all surviving Vinaya traditions. Curated parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral include the Theravāda Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Pc 63) and Parivāra (Pc 63), as well as the corresponding nun's rule in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pc 144) and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Pc 144) [SuttaCentral]. Full parallels are also preserved in the Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokkhas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records 437 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 104 texts, sharing substantial formulaic phrasing with the *Campeyyakkhandhaka* (Kd 9, especially §1.3–1.5 matching Kd 9 §2.2.1–2.2.2) and related Vibhaṅga rules on legal disputes and reproof (such as Pc 13, Pc 62, Pc 74, Pc 79, and Pc 82), as well as commentary in the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments with the Tibetan *Dul ba* (Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya), which confirms SuttaCentral's identified cross-tradition parallels [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
